+def _apply_table(s, table):
+    """
+    Apply a _replace_table to s. A replacement can only match when both of its
+    characters occur in s; present is a superset of the characters of s (the
+    initial ones plus every token minted so far, nothing is ever removed), so
+    skipping the others gives the same result without scanning s for them.
+    """
+    present = set(s)
+    for ps, c, a, b in table:
+        if a in present and b in present:
+            n = len(s)
+            s = s.replace(ps, c)
+            if len(s) != n:
+                present.add(c)
+    return s

+        app((chr(p0) + chr(p1), chr(idx)))

+# the first (most frequent) merges of a table match many times: str.replace
+# is cheapest there; later merges match rarely, and c.join(s.split(ps)) does
+# one scan of s instead of str.replace's two (count pass + replace pass)
+_SPLIT_FROM = 32
+
+
+def _apply_table(s, table):
+    """
+    Apply a _replace_table to s: every replacement in table order. str.split
+    finds the same left-to-right non-overlapping matches as str.replace, so
+    c.join(s.split(ps)) == s.replace(ps, c) (and is s itself without a match).
+    """
+    for ps, c in table[:_SPLIT_FROM]:
+        s = s.replace(ps, c)
+    for ps, c in table[_SPLIT_FROM:]:
+        s = c.join(s.split(ps))
+    return s
